newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin said happy at controversial telecoms deal.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin said happy at controversial telecoms deal.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin on Wednesday approved the handling of a controversial telecommunications privatisation which has sparked off a major public row in Russia, a top aide said.
First Deputy Prime Minister Anatoly Chubais told Interfax news agency: "B. Yeltsin is satisfied that the tender went according to the tough rules which had been laid down and followed."
He was speaking after briefing Yeltsin at his Volzhsky Utyos holiday residence in central Russia on a tender to sell off 25 percent of the Svyazinvest telecommunications giant.
The row has pitted reformist ministers against some of the influential media controlled by banks.
It flared up last week when it was announced that the 25 percent plus one share stake in Svyazinvest -- Russia's biggest privatisation -- was won by a consortium built around Uneximbank.
The bank, Russia's third biggest, is headed by Vladimir Potanin, who was a first deputy prime minister until March.

It was backed by several foreign entities, including Deutsche Morgan Grenfell (DMG), the London-based investment banking division of Germany's Deutsche Bank, billionaire financier George Soros, and U.S. asset management group Morgan Stanley Asset Management.
Participants in the losing consortium have not been officially named.

But Potanin and the Russian media have said they were Vladimir Gusinsky, founder of the Most financial and industrial group, and tycoon Boris Berezovsky, who has formally dropped his business roles to take up a Kremlin post.

Powerful media organisations controlled by the two men's business groups have launched a bitter attack on the Svyazinvest deal, saying it was a shadowy affair between state officials and financial magnates.
Ministers have denied any wrongdoing and First Deputy Prime Minister Boris Nemtsov called the media reaction "hysterical".
